name: @southleft/al-web-components
description: The Web Component powered design system for web applications

..//: The JS chunk is RENAMED by rollup (vite.config.mjs:185 maps the `bundle` entry to components/bundle/bundle.js), but tsc emits the declaration from the SOURCE layout — components/bundle.ts -> dist/components/bundle.d.ts. `types` pointed at the renamed JS directory, where no .d.ts has ever existed, so every TypeScript consumer of the root import silently got `any`. Do not 'tidy' these two into the same directory: bundle.d.ts re-exports './ALElement' and './<component>/<component>' relative to dist/components/, and moving it one level deeper breaks all 1,652 of those paths.

./theme-engine.//: The deterministic OKLCH theme engine (buildTheme/applyTheme + the OKLCH/WCAG primitives). A single barrel, deliberately NOT a wildcard: the sub-modules behind it (engine, oklch, ramps, personalities, apply, constants, types) are bundled into one chunk by vite.config.mjs and have no stable dist paths of their own. Until now this lived in `.storybook/ai-theme/`, where a dot-directory kept it out of the tsc program and out of the Vite entry map — so it was never compiled, never declared, never packed, and no consumer of this package could derive a theme. The `types`/`default` split mirrors `./motion`: same source layout, same emit.

scripts.build: npm run build:tokens && npm run build:icons && npm run build:custom-elements.json && del-cli dist && vite build -c vite.config.mjs && tsc && node ../../scripts/copy-assets-to-dist.js
scripts.//build:tokens: build-tokens-digest.mjs is the LAST step here, not in build:custom-elements.json, because its only input is styles/dist/tokens.json — written by copy-tokens-to-legacy-dist.js on the line before. Wiring it to the CEM build instead would make `pnpm --filter @southleft/al-web-components build:custom-elements.json` (which CI runs standalone) crash on a fresh clone.
scripts.build:custom-elements.json: cem analyze --config custom-elements-manifest.config.mjs --outdir . && node ../../scripts/generate-component-schemas.js && node ../../scripts/generate-schema-index.js && node ../../scripts/ai-readiness/build-cem-digest.mjs

//sideEffects: Two sets of paths, and BOTH are load-bearing. The `./dist/**` entries are for consumers of the PUBLISHED package. The `./components/**` / `./directives/**` entries are for anything that bundles this package FROM SOURCE — which is what `story-fixture/` does, and what both Storybooks did before they were deleted (2026-08-25). Without them, Rollup treats every bare `import './button'` as side-effect-free and DROPS IT, so `customElements.define` never runs and a production build renders every component as unstyled text (dev is unaffected: Vite does not tree-shake). Measured on the Storybook build before the fix: 2 surviving `customElements.define` calls in the whole preview bundle. The `.storybook/auto-registry.ts` entry went with the directory; `story-fixture/iframe.html` sets `window.alAutoRegistry` inline in <head> instead, which is the documented registration path and not subject to tree-shaking at all. NOTE the glob shapes: `./components/*/*.ts` and `./components/icon/icons/*.ts` are enumerated rather than a blanket `./components/**` precisely so `components/icon/phosphor/**` (1,512 generated glyph modules) stays side-effect-free and tree-shakeable, which is the same split `vite.config.mjs` maintains for the built chunks.
